region.text: Hisn Kayfa (Hasankeyf), the Artuqid iqta' on the Tigris

ledger.note: 1102: the Seljuk sultan grants Hisn Kayfa (Hasankeyf) to the Artuqids as an iqta'; the Hasankeyf page: the sultan 'granted Hisn Kayfa as a iqtâ' to the Artuqids in 1101/1102'; the Artuqids infobox gives 1102 as the foundation. The year is the page's own, but it is given as 1101/1102.

region.text: Mardin and the plain to Nusaybin (Nisibin)

ledger.note: 1108: Ilghazi takes Mardin. 'Ilghazi took Mardin from Ibrahim, son of Sökmen' (the page's infobox gives 1107; the Artuqids lead gives 1106). The loser is Artuqid kin, so the dynasty's total land changes only if Mardin is not already counted as Artuqid.
1117: Ilghazi gains control of Aleppo after Lu'lu's assassination (Ilghazi page; the Artuqids narrative says 1118, its Aleppo section 1117-1128).

ledger.counterpart: holder not named by the page
ledger.note: 1118: Ilghazi takes Mayyafariqin and pacifies the surrounding countryside (Ilghazi page); the page does not name the previous holder.

region.text: Atharib, Zerdana, Sarmin, Ma'arrat al-Numan and Kafr Tab (circles as in the principality-of-antioch dossier)

ledger.note: 1119: Ager Sanguinis (28 June) hands the Antiochene frontier towns to Ilghazi. 'Atharib, Zerdana, Sarmin, Ma'arrat al-Numan and Kafr Tab rapidly fell into Muslim hands' after the Antiochene army was annihilated; the page calls Ilghazi 'the Artuqid ruler of Aleppo' and the result 'Artuqid victory'.

region.text: Atharib, Zerdana, Sarmin, Ma'arrat al-Numan and Kafr Tab (circles as in the principality-of-antioch dossier)

ledger.note: 1119: Baldwin II recovers the lost towns after winning at Hab on 14 August. 'Subsequently, Baldwin recovered some of the lost towns' (Ager Sanguinis page); the page does not say which. All five are returned together; the principality-of-antioch dossier mirrors this.

ledger.counterpart: holder not named by the page
ledger.note: 1120: Ilghazi takes Nisibin (Nusaybin) (Ilghazi page); the page does not name the previous holder. Inside the Mardin disc of the keyframes.
1128: Zengi takes Aleppo. 'Zengi took Aleppo' (Artuqids page); Aleppo then 'ruled by the Zengid dynasty until 1183'.

region.text: Harput (Kharput), the Artuqid branch of Harput

ledger.note: 1185: Harput becomes an independent Artuqid principality under Imad ud-din Abu Bakr (1185-1204). 'Harput became independent from Kara Arslan's line.' The page does not say when the Artuqids first held Harput.

ledger.counterpart: holder not named by the page
ledger.note: 1198: the Hasankeyf branch conquers Amid (Diyarbakir) (Artuqids page); the page does not name the previous holder, and also dates the move of the Hasankeyf capital to Diyarbakir to 1183.

union.text: Hisn Kayfa (Hasankeyf), the Artuqid iqta' on the Tigris

ledger.note: 1231: the Ayyubids demolish the Hasankeyf centre after its ruler tried to ally with the Seljuks. 'demolished by the Ayyubids in 1231' (Artuqids page); the Hasankeyf page has the city captured only in November 1232.
1232: Amid (Diyarbakir) surrenders. Al-Mas'ud, the Artuqid prince 'who controlled Amida and Hisn Kayfa', was taken captive and by 18 October 1232 'surrendered Amida to al-Kamil'.

region.text: Hisn Kayfa (Hasankeyf), the Artuqid iqta' on the Tigris

ledger.note: 1232: Hasankeyf falls to al-Kamil. 'The city was captured only in Safar 630/November 1232'; al-Kamil installed as-Salih Ayyub as governor. The Artuqids infobox lists the Hasankeyf territories as an Ayyubid vassal in 1232.

union.text: Hisn Kayfa (Hasankeyf), the Artuqid iqta' on the Tigris

ledger.note: 1232: the Ayyubid campaign ends with the capture of Hasankeyf in November.

region.text: Harput (Kharput), the Artuqid branch of Harput

ledger.note: 1234: Kayqubad I, Seljuk sultan of Rum, conquers Harput and ends the Harput branch (Artuqids page; its lead gives 1233 as the end of independence).

union.text: Mardin and the plain to Nusaybin (Nisibin)

ledger.note: 1409: the Qara Qoyunlu conquer Mardin, ending Artuqid rule; Qara Muhammad had received the submission of Majd al-Din Isa in 1384. The qara-qoyunlu dossier mirrors this under the counterpart 'Artuqids of Mardin'.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Four pages opened (Artuqids, Ilghazi, Hasankeyf, Ager Sanguinis). Wikidata id not obtainable (wikidata.org unreachable): null.
Disagreements between pages, all recorded in the notes of the events: foundation 1101/1102 (Hasankeyf page) vs 1102 (Artuqids infobox); Mardin taken 1108 (Ilghazi text) / 1107 (Ilghazi infobox) / 1106 (Artuqids lead, 'Mardin branch 1101-1409' elsewhere on the same page); Aleppo 1117 vs 1118; Hasankeyf capital moved to Diyarbakir in 1183 but Diyarbakir conquered 1198; Ayyubid demolition of Hasankeyf 1231 vs capture 1232.
Not settled: the Artuqids of Jerusalem (Artuk governor from 1086, Sökmen and Ilghazi expelled in 1098 by the Fatimid vizier) are before the 1102 foundation and are not drawn; the fatimid-caliphate dossier's 1098 gain of Jerusalem names 'Artuqids' as counterpart and should name seljuks-of-syria (Tutush's appointee) instead. When the Artuqids first held Harput and Nisibin's later tenure are not on any page opened. The Mardin line after 1234 (Il-Khanate, Timurid, Qara Qoyunlu, later Aq Qoyunlu) is only partly on the Artuqids page.
Vassal relations of the Artuqids belong to the suzerains' dossiers: zengid-dynasty (Nur al-Din Zengi 1146-1174, 'the Artuqids became his vassals'), ayyubid-sultanate (Saladin; Hasankeyf as vassal 1232 on the infobox), ilkhanate / mongol-empire (Qara Arslan submitted to Hulegu c. 1260), timurid-empire, qara-qoyunlu (already carries 1384-1409 as 'Artuqids of Mardin'). None of those is mirrored here.
Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Hasankeyf, Mayyafariqin (Silvan).
Rulers list omitted: the page gives separate lists for three branches.
